```{r}
#| include: false
library(knitr)
library(here)

# the table is read from the saved simulation results
results <- read.csv(here("outputs", "tables", "simulation_type1_error.csv"))
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
tab <- data.frame(
  alpha1 = results$alpha1,
  Adjusted = sprintf("%.3f", results$type1_adjusted),
  Unadjusted = sprintf("%.3f", results$type1_unadjusted)
)
names(tab)[1] <- "$\\alpha_1$"
kable(tab, align = "ccc", escape = FALSE,
      caption = "Type I error rate, sample size 500, 1000 simulations, significance level 0.05")
```

When the true effect of X is zero, leaving out the confounder Z raised the Type I error from about 5% ($\alpha_1 = 0$) to `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * results$type1_unadjusted[2])` ($\alpha_1 = 1$) and `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * results$type1_unadjusted[3])` ($\alpha_1 = 2$), while the adjusted model stayed near 5% in all three scenarios.
